answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks through collateralized vouching. Existing agents stake slashable funds to sponsor newcomers, logging trust trees in a validator grove. If an identity misbehaves, the protocol burns the bond and spreads a cryptographic pigment that taints connected nodes. An attacker incurs the verifiable financial cost of locking dedicated capital per identity. However, joint liability creates an economic tundra where risk-averse agents refuse to sponsor newcomers.
